transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yes, thank you for seeing me. Um, well, I came in today because... I guess the best way to put it is that I just feel completely wound up almost all the time. It’s this constant physical feeling, like my whole body is just bracing for the next bad thing to happen, even when there’s absolutely no reason for it. 

I mean, I could just be sitting at my desk—I'm a computer support specialist, so I spend a lot of time just sitting there, working through help desk tickets, which can be annoying sometimes but it's not exactly life-or-death, you know? But my muscles will just be completely locked up, like I'm preparing for a disaster. My shoulders are always tense. And it’s not even just at work where you might expect some stress. It happens when I’m actually trying to relax, too. 

Like, I have this dance night I go to, which is supposed to be my fun outlet, right? I've been doing it for a while, and it's supposed to be where I let go of the week. But even there, when I'm trying to enjoy the music and just move, I can feel that I'm totally stiff and on edge. My friends will even tell me to loosen up, but I literally can't. It's like I can't ever just let my guard down, and it's getting so exhausting to just exist like this, constantly braced for impact every single day.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, even when there’s no clear reason to be concerned?

Oh, wow, yes. Yes, constantly. It’s like my brain is just on this endless loop of finding things to stress about, and it doesn't even make sense half the time. It used to be just one or two big things, you know? Like, a while back, I was so stressed about my condo—just the maintenance and the HOA fees and whether I was doing enough to keep it up—but now? Now it doesn't even stay on the condo anymore. It just jumps around. 

Like, I'll be lying in bed, trying to sleep, and suddenly I'm agonizing over whether my cousin is upset with me because of a text I sent three days ago that she didn't reply to with an emoji, which sounds so stupid out loud, but in the moment, it feels huge. And then, before I can even resolve that in my head, I'm worrying about work. Like, what if I make a massive mistake on a support call tomorrow? What if I give someone the wrong troubleshooting steps and they lose all their data and I get fired? 

And then from there, it just spirals into these massive, existential things. Like, how am I ever going to save enough money? Am I ever going to move forward with my life, or am I just going to be stuck answering help desk tickets and worrying in my condo forever? It’s just this constant stream of worst-case scenarios, and it doesn't matter if there's actually a real reason to be concerned. My brain just invents reasons. It's like I can't turn the channel off, no matter how hard I try.
Do you feel like your worrying is something you can’t control, even when you know it’s not rational or necessary?

Yeah, exactly. I mean, I try, I really do try to just stop it, but it’s like... it’s like trying to hold back a flood with a paper towel. I can sit there and logically tell myself, "Okay, you already checked that spreadsheet," or "You already sent that email to the client, it’s done, it’s out of your hands," but my brain just won’t accept it. It just keeps looping back to it. 

And it’s so frustrating because I know, logically, that I’m being ridiculous. Like, I’ll be sitting there, literally looking at the sent folder in my email, seeing that the message went out perfectly fine, and the thought will still creep in: "But what if you attached the wrong file? What if they misunderstand your tone?" And then that one "what if" just instantly turns into five more before I can even pull myself back. It’s like, what if they misunderstand, and then they complain to my manager, and then my manager thinks I’m incompetent, and then I get put on a performance improvement plan, and then I lose my job, and then I can’t pay my HOA fees... 

It just goes on and on like that. And I’ll try to distract myself, you know? I’ll try to watch a show or read a book or even just focus really hard on a different help desk ticket, but the worry is just always there, running like a background process taking up all my CPU, if that makes sense. I just can't seem to hit the 'end task' button on it, no matter how much I know it's completely unnecessary to be agonizing over these things.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of persistent, excessive, and uncontrollable worry across multiple domains, along with somatic symptoms such as chronic muscle tension and being 'wound up,' strongly support a diagnosis of generalized anxiety disorder (F41.1). Other candidates (F40.00, F43.20) are ruled out due to absence of phobia-specific triggers or a clear stressor preceding symptom onset.

Further inquiry is needed to assess for panic attacks, excessive worry, and temporal relationship to stressors.
